title: The Influence of Spraying Parameters and Powder Sizes on the Microstructure and Mechanical Behavior of Cold-Sprayed Inconel 625 Deposits
InformationInFigures: Yes. Porosity in Fig. 8. UTS in Fig. 9

preSprayedProperties.Majority_Powder_Source: PRAXAIR Surface Technologies, Indianapolis, Indiana, USA
preSprayedProperties.Powder_Morphology: Well separated and spherical, with small satellite particles. contains cellular dendrites with side branches and Nb segregation in interdendritic regions.
preSprayedProperties.Substrate_Surface_Preparation: grit-blasted with #200 mesh alumina particles at room temperature at a pressure of 6 bar and at an impact angle of 45 degrees.

experimentalProperties.Particle_Critical_Velocity_Source: Calculated with KSS-software (Kinetic Spray Solutions GmbH, Buchholz, Germany)
experimentalProperties.Additional_Manufacturing_Processes_Descr: The deposition had to be interrupted every ten layers for grit blasting to clean the nozzle and to avoid nozzle clogging. For this, a second powder feeder loaded with Al2O3 with the trade name EK180 (Wiwox, Erkrath, Germany) was used. Such refreshing of the nozzle was performed at a spray gun position sufficiently far away from the part in front of the exhaust system to avoid any influence on the already deposited material.  The full deposits were processed as a sequence of 35 layers. For preparing coating cross sections, deposited samples were hot mounted in a conductive resin and polished using standard metallographic techniques down to OPS (oxide polishing suspension, 0.05 μm) as the final finish.

resultsValues.Microstructural_Features: dense with low porosity, less than 2%, with no cracking or delamination at the interface to the substrate. basic features of the powder microstructures after etching the polished-cross-section such as dendritic or grain refined areas, were also observed inside the deformed particles. However, they are mostly elongated due to the high particle deformation. highly elongated grains are observed close to interparticle boundaries. also presence of some pores and non-bonded interfaces at the particle-particle interfaces. larger microporosities with increasing powder size.

Experiments.Notes: n-val: 0.95. This is standard powder (medium size). some nozzle dimensions given as: a 100 mm pre-chamber length, corresponding to a powder injection at 128 mm upstream of the nozzle throat, and an expansion ratio of 5.6. (unsure where to put this)
